title: Evidence-based examination signs (likelihood ratios) for the web and iOS Bayesian engines
reference: McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (2022) and the JAMA Rational Clinical Examination series. Every value is fromMemory until checked against the source (docs/clinical-validation/changes/evidence-exam.md, Needs sign-off).
conversion: Sensitivity and specificity are derived from the likelihood ratios: specificity = (LR+ - 1) / (LR+ - LR-), sensitivity = LR+ x (1 - specificity). A second target (alsoTargets) shares the primary target's specificity: its sensitivity = its LR+ x (1 - specificity), capped at 0.95. iOS: logLR = round(5 x ln LR).

engineModes.lr: The sign is its own engine feature with these likelihood ratios; it supersedes (drops) the listed free-text twin features when the chip is recorded, so the sign counts once.
engineModes.twin: A red-flag or severity sign: 'present' records the listed engine features (the engine's own, safety-tuned weighting); the likelihood ratio is shown but not applied; absence is never used.
engineModes.none: Low value or no usable likelihood ratio: documentation only; it does not change the differential.

absencePolicy: An absent sign updates the engines only when negativeMeaningful is true and the chip was set to 'absent' (examined and absent). Unrecorded signs are never read as absent.

abdominal-wall.label: Abdominal-wall pain (e.g. anterior cutaneous nerve entrapment)

heart-failure.label: Heart failure (raised filling pressure or low ejection fraction)

supraclavicular-malignancy.label: Malignancy draining to the supraclavicular fossa (upper GI, breast, thyroid, lymphoma)

signs.name: Murphy's sign
signs.elicit: Press under the right costal margin at the mid-clavicular line and ask for a deep breath: positive if the breath stops short because of pain.
signs.source: Trowbridge RL et al. Does this patient have acute cholecystitis? JAMA 2003;289:80-86 (Rational Clinical Examination); McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), Abdominal pain and tenderness
signs.note: Less sensitive in older and diabetic patients (sonographic Murphy's sign is a different test).

signs.name: McBurney's point tenderness
signs.elicit: Press one-third of the way from the right anterior superior iliac spine to the umbilicus: positive if that point is maximally tender.
signs.source: McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), Abdominal pain and tenderness (appendicitis)

signs.name: Rovsing's sign
signs.elicit: Press deeply in the left iliac fossa: positive if the pain is felt in the right iliac fossa.
signs.source: Wagner JM et al. Does this patient have appendicitis? JAMA 1996;276:1589-94 (RCE); McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022)
signs.note: A negative Rovsing's sign barely changes the probability (LR- 0.8).

signs.name: Psoas sign
signs.elicit: With the patient on the left side, extend the right hip (or ask for hip flexion against resistance): positive if this provokes right lower abdominal pain.
signs.source: Wagner JM et al. JAMA 1996;276:1589-94 (RCE); McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022)
signs.note: Insensitive: its absence does not argue against appendicitis.

signs.name: Obturator sign
signs.elicit: With hip and knee flexed to 90 degrees, rotate the hip internally: positive if this provokes hypogastric pain.
signs.source: McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), Abdominal pain and tenderness
signs.note: Low value: no pooled estimate, and the studies that exist find likelihood ratios not different from 1. Recorded for documentation only; it does not change the differential.

signs.name: Rebound tenderness
signs.elicit: Press slowly and deeply, then release quickly: positive if the pain is worse on release.
signs.source: McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), Abdominal pain and tenderness (peritonitis)
signs.note: Percussion tenderness gives the same information more gently.

signs.name: Percussion tenderness
signs.elicit: Percuss gently over each quadrant: positive if percussion is painful over the site of pain.
signs.source: McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), Abdominal pain and tenderness (peritonitis)

signs.name: Guarding
signs.elicit: Palpate gently: positive if the abdominal muscles tighten under the hand over the painful area.
signs.source: McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), Abdominal pain and tenderness (peritonitis)
signs.note: Blunted in the elderly, on steroids and after opioids.

signs.name: Rigidity (board-like abdomen)
signs.elicit: Palpate gently: positive if the abdominal wall is continuously rigid and does not relax, even with distraction.
signs.source: McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), Abdominal pain and tenderness (peritonitis)
signs.note: Specific but insensitive: a soft abdomen does not exclude peritonitis.

signs.name: Carnett's sign (abdominal-wall tenderness test)
signs.elicit: Find the tender point, then ask the patient to lift the head and shoulders off the bed: positive if the tenderness stays the same or increases with the muscles tensed.
signs.source: Takada T et al. Carnett's sign in chronic abdominal pain, J Gen Intern Med 2011; McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022) (positive test argues against peritonitis, LR 0.1)
signs.note: A positive test points to the abdominal wall (e.g. anterior cutaneous nerve entrapment) rather than a viscus; McGee gives LR 0.1 for peritonitis when positive. Values come from single cohorts.

signs.name: Shifting dullness
signs.elicit: Percuss from the umbilicus to the flank until dull, keep the finger there and roll the patient away: positive if the dull note becomes resonant.
signs.source: Williams JW Jr, Simel DL. Does this patient have ascites? JAMA 1992;267:2645-8 (RCE); McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022)
signs.note: Finding-level sign: it changes the probability of ascites, which then weighs the causes of ascites (cirrhosis, malignancy, heart failure). Needs about 500 mL of fluid.

signs.name: Fluid wave (fluid thrill)
signs.elicit: With the patient's (or an assistant's) hand edge pressed along the midline, tap one flank: positive if the impulse is felt at the other flank.
signs.source: Williams JW Jr, Simel DL. JAMA 1992;267:2645-8 (RCE); McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022)

signs.name: Palpable non-tender gallbladder in a jaundiced patient (Courvoisier)
signs.elicit: In a jaundiced patient, palpate below the right costal margin at the lateral edge of rectus: positive if a smooth, non-tender, pear-shaped mass moves with respiration.
signs.source: McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), The liver and gallbladder (palpable gallbladder: extrahepatic obstruction in jaundice)
signs.note: Stones rarely distend a chronically fibrosed gallbladder, so a palpable gallbladder points to a malignant distal obstruction. Its absence means little.

signs.name: Obstructive (high-pitched, tinkling) bowel sounds
signs.elicit: Listen for at least a minute in the mid-abdomen: positive if the sounds are high-pitched, tinkling or come in rushes with colic.
signs.source: Böhner H et al. Simple data from history and physical examination help to exclude bowel obstruction, Eur J Surg 1998; McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022) (abnormal bowel sounds: likelihood ratio not significant for peritonitis)
signs.note: Low value: bowel sounds barely change the probability of obstruction, and absent or normal bowel sounds never exclude peritonitis or obstruction.

signs.name: Widened expansile aortic pulsation
signs.elicit: Place both hands either side of the aortic pulsation above the umbilicus: positive if the hands are pushed apart and the width is 3 cm or more.
signs.source: Lederle FA, Simel DL. Does this patient have abdominal aortic aneurysm? JAMA 1999;281:77-82 (RCE, AAA 4 cm or more)
signs.note: Insensitive in obesity: a normal examination does not exclude an aneurysm. Documented 'pulsatile mass' in the notes is counted separately (not superseded).

signs.name: Cough impulse
signs.elicit: With the patient standing, place fingers over the swelling and ask for a cough: positive if an expansile impulse is felt.
signs.source: van den Berg JC et al. Detection of groin hernia with physical examination, ultrasound and MRI compared with laparoscopic findings, Invest Radiol 1999; HerniaSurge Group, Hernia 2018
signs.note: An incarcerated hernia loses its cough impulse, so an absent impulse does not argue against a hernia (it may mean incarceration).

signs.name: Swelling reduces completely
signs.elicit: With the patient lying, apply gentle pressure over the swelling: positive if it disappears completely.
signs.source: WSES guidelines for emergency repair of complicated abdominal wall hernias (Birindelli et al. World J Emerg Surg 2017); HerniaSurge Group, Hernia 2018
signs.note: No accuracy study: the likelihood ratios are estimates for sign-off. 'Absent' (irreducible) is recorded as an irreducible hernia, which the engine weighs towards incarceration; a tense, tender, irreducible hernia is incarcerated until proven otherwise.

signs.name: Groin lump above and medial to the pubic tubercle
signs.elicit: Find the pubic tubercle and trace the neck of the swelling: positive if the neck lies above and medial to the tubercle (inguinal canal).
signs.source: HerniaSurge Group. International guidelines for groin hernia management, Hernia 2018; McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022)
signs.note: No pooled accuracy estimate; examination often misclassifies femoral hernias as inguinal. Record the paired sign (below and lateral) rather than 'absent'.

signs.name: Groin lump below and lateral to the pubic tubercle
signs.elicit: Find the pubic tubercle and trace the neck of the swelling: positive if the neck lies below the inguinal ligament and lateral to the tubercle (femoral canal).
signs.source: HerniaSurge Group, Hernia 2018 (femoral hernia: women, older age, emergency presentation); McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022)
signs.note: Estimates for sign-off. A femoral hernia is repaired promptly because of its strangulation risk.

signs.name: Dullness to percussion
signs.elicit: Percuss symmetrically from apex to base on both sides: positive if one area is dull compared with the other side.
signs.source: Metlay JP et al. Does this patient have community-acquired pneumonia? JAMA 1997;278:1440-5 (RCE); McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), Pneumonia; Wong CL et al. Does this patient have a pleural effusion? JAMA 2009;301:309-17 (RCE)
signs.note: Also the best single sign of a pleural effusion (LR+ 8.7, Wong 2009).

signs.name: Crackles (crepitations)
signs.elicit: Auscultate both lungs, asking for deep breaths through the mouth: positive if fine or coarse crackles persist after a cough.
signs.source: Metlay JP et al. Does this patient have community-acquired pneumonia? JAMA 1997;278:1440-5 (RCE); McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), Pneumonia; Wang CS et al. Does this dyspneic patient in the emergency department have congestive heart failure? JAMA 2005;294:1944-56 (RCE)

signs.name: Reduced breath sounds
signs.elicit: Auscultate symmetrical zones: positive if breath sounds are clearly quieter on one side or zone.
signs.source: Metlay JP et al. Does this patient have community-acquired pneumonia? JAMA 1997;278:1440-5 (RCE); McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), Pneumonia; ATLS 10th ed. (American College of Surgeons 2018) for chest trauma
signs.note: The chest-trauma likelihood ratio is an estimate for sign-off.

signs.name: Egophony
signs.elicit: Ask the patient to say 'ee' while you auscultate: positive if it sounds like 'ay' over one area.
signs.source: Metlay JP et al. Does this patient have community-acquired pneumonia? JAMA 1997;278:1440-5 (RCE); McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), Pneumonia

signs.name: Bronchial breath sounds
signs.elicit: Auscultate: positive if breath sounds are harsh with a gap between inspiration and expiration over a peripheral zone.
signs.source: Metlay JP et al. Does this patient have community-acquired pneumonia? JAMA 1997;278:1440-5 (RCE); McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), Pneumonia

signs.name: Pleural rub
signs.elicit: Auscultate over the painful area: positive if a creaking, leathery sound is heard in both phases of respiration.
signs.source: McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), Pneumonia; Metlay JP et al. JAMA 1997 (not among the discriminating signs)
signs.note: Low value: specific for pleural inflammation (pneumonia, pulmonary infarction, serositis) but rare and without a usable likelihood ratio; recorded for documentation only.

signs.name: Raised jugular venous pressure
signs.elicit: At 45 degrees, measure the height of the internal jugular pulsation above the sternal angle: positive if more than 3 cm (CVP above 8 cm H2O).
signs.source: Wang CS et al. JAMA 2005;294:1944-56 (RCE, heart failure in the dyspnoeic ED patient); McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), The heart

signs.name: Third heart sound (S3 gallop)
signs.elicit: With the bell at the apex and the patient in the left lateral position: positive if a low-pitched sound follows S2.
signs.source: Wang CS et al. JAMA 2005;294:1944-56 (RCE, heart failure in the dyspnoeic ED patient); McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), The heart
signs.note: Specific but insensitive; inter-observer agreement is poor.

signs.name: Displaced apex beat
synonyms: apical impulse lateral to the mid-clavicular line
signs.elicit: Palpate the apex beat supine: positive if it lies lateral to the mid-clavicular line or is diffuse (more than 3 cm).
signs.source: McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), The heart (low ejection fraction)
signs.note: Detects left-ventricular dilatation (low ejection fraction) rather than acute decompensation.

signs.name: Hepatojugular (abdominojugular) reflux
signs.elicit: Press firmly over the mid-abdomen for 10-15 seconds: positive if the JVP rises by 3 cm or more and stays up.
signs.source: Wang CS et al. JAMA 2005;294:1944-56 (RCE, heart failure in the dyspnoeic ED patient); McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), The heart

signs.name: Calf swelling 3 cm or more (10 cm below the tibial tuberosity)
signs.elicit: Measure both calf circumferences 10 cm below the tibial tuberosity: positive if the symptomatic calf is 3 cm or more larger.
signs.source: Anand SS et al. Does this patient have deep vein thrombosis? JAMA 1998;279:1094-9 (RCE); Wells PS et al. NEJM 2003
signs.note: Individual leg signs are weak: use Wells DVT with a D-dimer. Recorded as unilateral leg swelling for the engine.

signs.name: Homans' sign
signs.elicit: Dorsiflex the ankle with the knee slightly flexed: positive if this causes calf pain.
signs.source: Anand SS et al. JAMA 1998;279:1094-9 (RCE)
signs.note: Low value: does not help diagnose or exclude DVT. Use Wells DVT and a D-dimer.

signs.name: Absent or reduced foot pulses
synonyms: absent dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses
signs.elicit: Palpate dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses on both feet: positive if either is absent or clearly weaker than the other side.
signs.source: Khan NA et al. Does the clinical examination predict lower extremity peripheral arterial disease? JAMA 2006;295:536-46 (RCE)
signs.note: The diabetic-foot likelihood ratio is an estimate for sign-off.

signs.name: Ankle-brachial pressure index below 0.9
signs.elicit: Hand-held Doppler: highest ankle systolic pressure divided by the higher brachial pressure; positive if below 0.9.
signs.source: Xu D et al. Sensitivity and specificity of the ankle-brachial index to diagnose peripheral artery disease, Vasc Med 2010; ESC/ESVS 2017 PAD guidelines
signs.note: Calcified arteries (diabetes, renal failure) give a falsely normal or high index (above 1.3): use toe pressures then.

signs.name: Capillary refill longer than 3 seconds (adult)
signs.elicit: Press the fingertip at heart level for 5 seconds and release: positive if colour takes more than 3 seconds to return.
signs.source: McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), Hypovolaemia; McGee S et al. Is this patient hypovolemic? JAMA 1999;281:1022-9 (RCE)
signs.note: Low value for detecting hypovolaemia in adults (affected by temperature and age). Documentation only; use the observations and lactate.

signs.name: Hard, fixed or irregular breast lump
signs.elicit: Palpate with the flat of the fingers, arm raised then relaxed: positive if the lump is hard, has an irregular edge or is fixed to skin or chest wall.
signs.source: NICE NG12 (2015, updated 2023) suspected cancer; Association of Breast Surgery triple assessment guidance; McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), The breast
signs.note: A soft, mobile lump still needs triple assessment: absence is never reassurance. Fat necrosis mimics cancer.

signs.name: Skin tethering or dimpling over a breast lump
signs.elicit: Inspect with arms raised and hands pressed on hips; lift the breast gently: positive if the skin puckers or dimples over the lump.
signs.source: NICE NG12 (2015, updated 2023) suspected cancer; Association of Breast Surgery triple assessment guidance; McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), The breast
signs.note: Estimate for sign-off; fat necrosis and previous surgery can tether skin.

signs.name: Peau d'orange
signs.elicit: Inspect the breast skin in good light: positive if it is oedematous with prominent pores like orange peel.
signs.source: NICE NG12 (2015, updated 2023) suspected cancer; Association of Breast Surgery triple assessment guidance; McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), The breast
signs.note: Estimate for sign-off. Suggests locally advanced or inflammatory cancer; mastitis and abscess can cause skin oedema.

signs.name: New nipple retraction
signs.elicit: Ask when the nipple changed and inspect: positive if a previously everted nipple is newly pulled in (a central slit suggests duct ectasia).
signs.source: NICE NG12 (2015, updated 2023) suspected cancer; Association of Breast Surgery triple assessment guidance; McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), The breast
signs.note: Estimate for sign-off; duct ectasia also retracts the nipple.

signs.name: Hard or fixed thyroid nodule
signs.elicit: Palpate from behind with the neck slightly flexed, and ask the patient to swallow: positive if the nodule is stony hard or does not move freely.
signs.source: British Thyroid Association guidelines 2014; ATA 2015 thyroid nodule guidelines; McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), The thyroid and its disorders
signs.note: A soft nodule can still be malignant: ultrasound (U-grading) decides.

signs.name: Cervical lymphadenopathy with a thyroid nodule
signs.elicit: Palpate levels II-VI on both sides: positive if a firm node lies on the same side as the nodule.
signs.source: British Thyroid Association guidelines 2014; ATA 2015 thyroid nodule guidelines; McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), The thyroid and its disorders

signs.name: Pemberton's sign
signs.elicit: Ask the patient to raise both arms above the head for a minute: positive if the face becomes plethoric or the patient becomes breathless or stridulous.
signs.source: British Thyroid Association guidelines 2014; ATA 2015 thyroid nodule guidelines; McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), The thyroid and its disorders; Pemberton HS, Lancet 1946
signs.note: No accuracy study: suggests thoracic-inlet obstruction by a retrosternal goitre. CT neck and thorax decides.

signs.name: Lower border of the goitre not palpable
signs.elicit: Palpate the lower pole on swallowing: positive if you cannot get below it above the clavicles.
signs.source: British Thyroid Association guidelines 2014; ATA 2015 thyroid nodule guidelines; McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), The thyroid and its disorders
signs.note: No accuracy study: suggests retrosternal extension (with tracheal deviation or Pemberton's sign). Documentation only.

signs.name: Neck stiffness (nuchal rigidity)
signs.elicit: Supine, flex the neck passively to bring the chin to the chest: positive if there is resistance or pain.
signs.source: Thomas KE et al. The diagnostic accuracy of Kernig's sign, Brudzinski's sign, and nuchal rigidity in adults with suspected meningitis, Clin Infect Dis 2002;35:46-52; Attia J et al. Does this adult patient have acute meningitis? JAMA 1999;282:175-81 (RCE)
signs.note: Low sensitivity (about 30 %): its absence does not exclude meningitis. The engine keeps its safety weighting of documented neck stiffness; absence is never used.

signs.name: Kernig's sign
signs.elicit: With the hip flexed to 90 degrees, extend the knee: positive if extension is limited by pain or resistance.
signs.source: Thomas KE et al. The diagnostic accuracy of Kernig's sign, Brudzinski's sign, and nuchal rigidity in adults with suspected meningitis, Clin Infect Dis 2002;35:46-52; Attia J et al. Does this adult patient have acute meningitis? JAMA 1999;282:175-81 (RCE)
signs.note: Low value: sensitivity about 5 %; neither presence nor absence changes the probability of meningitis. Documentation only.

signs.name: Brudzinski's sign
signs.elicit: Flex the neck passively: positive if the hips and knees flex involuntarily.
signs.source: Thomas KE et al. The diagnostic accuracy of Kernig's sign, Brudzinski's sign, and nuchal rigidity in adults with suspected meningitis, Clin Infect Dis 2002;35:46-52; Attia J et al. Does this adult patient have acute meningitis? JAMA 1999;282:175-81 (RCE)
signs.note: Low value: sensitivity about 5 %; its absence never excludes meningitis. Documentation only.

signs.name: New focal deficit: facial droop, arm drift or speech disturbance
signs.elicit: Ask the patient to smile, hold both arms out with eyes closed for 10 seconds and repeat a sentence: positive if any one is abnormal.
signs.source: Kothari RU et al. Cincinnati Prehospital Stroke Scale, Ann Emerg Med 1999;33:373-8; Goldstein LB, Simel DL. Is this patient having a stroke? JAMA 2005;293:2391-402 (RCE)
signs.note: A red-flag sign: recorded as a focal deficit for the engine (its safety weighting); absence is never used to lower stroke, TIA or cord compression.

signs.name: Papilloedema
signs.elicit: Fundoscopy in a darkened room: positive if the disc margins are blurred with loss of venous pulsation and elevated discs.
signs.source: McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), The eye (optic disc); NICE NG228 (2023) headache red flags
signs.note: Specific but insensitive for raised intracranial pressure; no pooled likelihood ratio. Red-flag sign: recorded for the engine; absence is never used.

signs.name: Spider naevi
signs.elicit: Inspect the territory of the superior vena cava: positive if there are more than a few central arterioles with radiating vessels that blanch on central pressure.
signs.source: Udell JA et al. Does this patient with liver disease have cirrhosis? JAMA 2012;307:832-42 (RCE)

signs.name: Palmar erythema
signs.elicit: Inspect the palms: positive if the thenar and hypothenar eminences are mottled red.
signs.source: Udell JA et al. Does this patient with liver disease have cirrhosis? JAMA 2012;307:832-42 (RCE)

signs.name: Caput medusae
synonyms: dilated abdominal wall veins draining away from the umbilicus
signs.elicit: Inspect the abdominal wall; strip a vein to find its flow: positive if dilated veins radiate from the umbilicus with flow away from it.
signs.source: Udell JA et al. Does this patient with liver disease have cirrhosis? JAMA 2012;307:832-42 (RCE); McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022)
signs.note: Specific but uncommon; the estimate rests on few patients.

signs.name: Prolonged capillary refill (child)
signs.elicit: Warm room; press the fingertip at heart level for 5 seconds and release: positive if refill takes more than 2 seconds.
signs.source: Steiner MJ et al. Is this child dehydrated? JAMA 2004;291:2746-54 (RCE)
signs.note: The best single sign of 5 % dehydration in children aged 1 month to 5 years.

signs.name: Reduced skin turgor (child)
signs.elicit: Pinch a fold of abdominal skin and release: positive if it recoils slowly (tenting for more than 2 seconds).
signs.source: Steiner MJ et al. Is this child dehydrated? JAMA 2004;291:2746-54 (RCE)

signs.name: Abnormal (deep, acidotic) breathing (child)
signs.elicit: Watch the breathing at rest: positive if it is deep and rapid without other signs of respiratory distress.
signs.source: Steiner MJ et al. Is this child dehydrated? JAMA 2004;291:2746-54 (RCE)

signs.name: Dry axilla (adult)
signs.elicit: Feel the skin of the axilla with the back of the fingers: positive if it is completely dry.
signs.source: McGee S et al. Is this patient hypovolemic? JAMA 1999;281:1022-9 (RCE); McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), Hypovolaemia
signs.note: Studied in older patients admitted acutely; a moist axilla does not exclude dehydration.

signs.name: Postural pulse rise of 30/min or more (or unable to stand)
signs.elicit: Measure the pulse after 2 minutes supine and after 1 minute standing: positive if it rises by 30/min or more, or dizziness stops the patient standing.
signs.source: McGee S et al. Is this patient hypovolemic? JAMA 1999;281:1022-9 (RCE)
signs.note: Applies to large blood loss (630-1150 mL, venesection studies). For moderate loss the sensitivity is only about 22 %: a normal result does not exclude bleeding. Documentation and bedside use; not an engine input.

signs.name: Skin mottling (knees)
signs.elicit: Inspect the skin around the knees: positive if there is a patchy violaceous discolouration (score by extent, 0-5).
signs.source: Ait-Oufella H et al. Mottling score predicts survival in septic shock, Intensive Care Med 2011;37:801-7
signs.note: A prognostic sign of hypoperfusion (mortality rises with the mottling score), not a diagnostic test; recorded for the engine as mottled skin.

signs.name: New confusion
signs.elicit: Assess orientation, attention and the collateral history: positive if confusion is new (a qSOFA and NEWS2 criterion).
signs.source: Singer M et al. Sepsis-3, JAMA 2016;315:801-10; RCP NEWS2 (2017)
signs.note: A severity criterion, not a diagnostic sign; recorded for the engine as confusion.

signs.name: Shaking chills (rigors)
signs.elicit: Ask about or observe shaking chills: positive if there is uncontrollable shaking with teeth chattering, even under blankets.
signs.source: Coburn B et al. Does this adult patient with suspected bacteremia require blood cultures? JAMA 2012;308:502-11 (RCE)
signs.note: Raises the probability of bacteraemia; take blood cultures. Recorded for the engine as rigors.

signs.name: Palpable rectal mass on digital rectal examination
signs.elicit: Left lateral, knees flexed; examine the rectal wall through 360 degrees: positive if a hard, irregular or ulcerated mass is felt.
signs.source: NICE NG12 (2015, updated 2023) suspected cancer: rectal mass; ACPGBI colorectal cancer guidance 2017
signs.note: Only the lower rectum can be felt: a normal examination does not exclude colorectal cancer.

signs.name: Melaena on the glove
signs.elicit: Inspect the glove after digital rectal examination: positive if the stool is black, tarry and offensive.
signs.source: Srygley FD et al. Does this patient have a severe upper gastrointestinal bleed? JAMA 2012;307:1072-9 (RCE)
signs.note: Points to an upper-GI source; recorded for the engine as melaena.

signs.name: Hard, nodular or asymmetric prostate
signs.elicit: On digital rectal examination feel both lobes and the median sulcus: positive if a lobe is hard, nodular, craggy or the sulcus is lost.
signs.source: Hoogendam A et al. Accuracy of digital rectal examination for prostate cancer, Fam Pract 1999; NICE NG12
signs.note: The web model has no prostate-cancer node, so on the web this is shown with its likelihood ratio but does not change the differential.

signs.name: Reduced anal tone or saddle anaesthesia
signs.elicit: Test perianal pinprick sensation and resting and squeeze tone on digital rectal examination: positive if either is reduced.
signs.source: GIRFT national cauda equina syndrome pathway (2023); NICE CKS back pain
signs.note: Red-flag sign; a normal examination does not exclude early cauda equina syndrome (MRI decides). Recorded for the engine; absence is never used.

signs.name: Right-sided rectal tenderness
signs.elicit: On digital rectal examination press towards the right pelvic wall: positive if this is painful.
signs.source: McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), Abdominal pain and tenderness (appendicitis); Wagner JM et al. JAMA 1996
signs.note: Low value: rectal tenderness does not help diagnose appendicitis. Documentation only.

signs.name: Lymph node larger than 2 cm
signs.elicit: Measure the node in two dimensions: positive if the largest is more than 2 cm (area 4 cm² or more).
signs.source: McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), Peripheral lymphadenopathy (Vassilakopoulos TP et al., Oncologist 2000; Fijten GH, Blijham GH, J Fam Pract 1988)
signs.note: The larger the node the higher the likelihood ratio (area 9 cm² or more: about 8). Nodes under 1 cm argue against malignancy.

signs.name: Hard lymph node
signs.elicit: Palpate the node: positive if it is stony hard (not rubbery or soft).
signs.source: McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), Peripheral lymphadenopathy (Vassilakopoulos TP et al., Oncologist 2000; Fijten GH, Blijham GH, J Fam Pract 1988)

signs.name: Fixed (matted) lymph node
signs.elicit: Try to move the node over deep structures and under the skin: positive if it is fixed or matted to other nodes.
signs.source: McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), Peripheral lymphadenopathy (Vassilakopoulos TP et al., Oncologist 2000; Fijten GH, Blijham GH, J Fam Pract 1988)

signs.name: Supraclavicular lymph node
signs.elicit: From behind, palpate both supraclavicular fossae while the patient does a Valsalva manoeuvre: positive if a node is felt.
signs.source: McGee S. Evidence-Based Physical Diagnosis, 5th ed. (Elsevier 2022), Peripheral lymphadenopathy (Vassilakopoulos TP et al., Oncologist 2000; Fijten GH, Blijham GH, J Fam Pract 1988)
signs.note: A left supraclavicular node points to an abdominal (upper-GI, pancreatic) primary; a right one to the chest or oesophagus.
